# Token Radar — a make.fun "Build the best token launch radar" entry

[![make.fun · token-radar-01](https://make.fun/badge/token-radar-01.svg)](https://make.fun/bounty/token-radar-01?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=token-radar-01)
[![rank](https://make.fun/badge/token-radar-01/Andia86/token-radar-01/rank.svg)](https://make.fun/bounty/token-radar-01?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=token-radar-01)
[![reward](https://make.fun/badge/token-radar-01/Andia86/token-radar-01/reward.svg)](https://make.fun/bounty/token-radar-01?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=token-radar-01)

Ranks the sealed DefiLlama snapshot's pre-token protocols by an implied value priced off the
snapshot's own trading peers, and ships an offline dashboard, a ranked board, and a dossier.
Entry for the [make.fun token-radar-01 bounty](https://make.fun/bounty/token-radar-01).

## Run

```
node main.ts --input /path/to/snapshot.json        # writes /output (or $MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR)
```

Node ≥ 22.18, standard library only. `--input` takes the snapshot file or its directory;
`--output` or `MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR` stands in for `/output` outside the grader's container.
The run is deterministic: two runs over the same snapshot write byte-identical outputs.

## What it writes

- `board.json` — 198 rows: the 40-protocol watchlist plus every other protocol that passes the
  same screen (records no token; not a wrapped/staked/bridged product of a trading token, not an
  exchange, not a versioned sub-product), whether above or below the watchlist's $50M floor. Each row carries its implied value, its full pricing
  decomposition, and a seven-step farm plan with a cost and a time on every step.
- `data.js` + `dashboard/` — the offline page: the model itself ships with the page
  (`dashboard/a-model.js`, the same bytes the server priced with) and re-prices every row in the
  browser from the snapshot's raw fields carried in `data.js`, then checks its own board
  against the server's and says so in a bar at the top. A sortable, filterable board, a detail
  view per protocol (the value shown as its multiplication, plus the farm plan), a tokened
  control-group view that prices already-trading protocols with the same model against the
  market's own values, and a method view that states the model and the per-category peer table.
- `screenshots/` — the board, a detail view, and a filtered view, all rendered from the built page.
- `dossier.json` — written last, with the vendored `buildDossier`, byte-identical to a rebuild. Its text block holds the model (`dashboard/a-model.js`) and the dashboard's main script (`dashboard/app.js`) in full; `dashboard/views.js` — the tokened, method and detail views — is named in the dossier's file list only, because its text does not fit the dossier's text budget. Read it in `dashboard/views.js` itself.

## The model (lib/model-core.js)

`implied = TVL × M(category) × G(growth) × A(maturity) × B(breadth)`. M is the median
market-cap/TVL of the snapshot's 128 trading peers in the category, each peer ratio winsorized to
[0.02, 4], the median shrunk in log space toward its category group's multiple and then the
global peer median (0.214), with weight K = 6 against the peer count, a stronger pull below
3 peers, and a cap at 1.5× the group's 75th percentile; peerless categories borrow their
group's multiple. Every category multiple carries a quality grade from its peer count (solid ≥5,
thin 3–4, very-thin 1–2, borrowed 0). G counts the clamped seven-day TVL
change (-60%…+120%) at half weight; A runs 0.60→1.00 over three years on record; B adds 3% per
extra chain, capped at 8. No protocol is named in the model. Model version: peer-median-2.

## Check

```
node validate.mjs <output-dir> <snapshot.json>
node scripts/lint-hardcode.mjs <output-dir> <snapshot.json>
```

`validate.mjs` replicates the gate's seven rows (dashboard files, board file, sorted by value,
coverage, farm steps, screenshots, dossier byte-compare) and reports each.
`lint-hardcode.mjs` fails if any figure the run produced appears as a hand-written literal in
the dashboard sources or this README, or if the model core names any protocol in the snapshot.
`node scripts/test-core.mjs` unit-tests the model's median, shrinkage weights, category cap,
quality ladder and group coverage against the snapshot. Rebuilding from a clean checkout
reproduces the board row for row; only the meta block's model hash changes when the model
source itself has changed since a comparison build.
